citation: Radhakrishnan SK, den Besten W, Deshaies RJ. p97-dependent retrotranslocation and proteolytic processing govern formation of active Nrf1 upon proteasome inhibition. eLife. 2014;3:e01856. doi:10.7554/eLife.01856.
description: This paper shows that proteasome inhibition allows Nrf1/NFE2L1 to escape degradation, undergo p97-dependent processing, and activate proteasome gene transcription. It supports interpreting up-regulated proteasome subunit or proteasome-associated transcripts after Psmb4 or Pomp loss as a proteasome bounce-back response.

citation: Hamazaki J, Murata S. ER-Resident Transcription Factor Nrf1 Regulates Proteasome Expression and Beyond. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2020;21(10):3683. doi:10.3390/ijms21103683.
description: This review summarizes the mammalian Nrf1/NFE2L1 pathway that coordinately induces proteasome subunit genes when proteasome function is impaired. It provides mechanistic context for proteasome-subunit up-regulation in the proteasome-assembly and proteasome-core perturbations.

citation: Poli MC, Ebstein F, Nicholas SK, et al. Heterozygous Truncating Variants in POMP Escape Nonsense-Mediated Decay and Cause a Unique Immune Dysregulatory Syndrome. American Journal of Human Genetics. 2018;102(6):1126-1142. doi:10.1016/j.ajhg.2018.04.010.
description: This study documents that POMP is a proteasome assembly chaperone required for incorporation of catalytic beta subunits into the proteasome. It supplies the POMP-to-proteasome-impairment step used with the NFE2L1 bounce-back literature.

citation: Czermak P, Amman F, Jantsch MF, Cimatti L. Organ-wide profiling in mouse reveals high editing levels of Filamin B mRNA in the musculoskeletal system. RNA Biology. 2018;15(7):877-885. doi:10.1080/15476286.2018.1480252.
description: This mouse study identifies ADAR2/ADARB1 as the enzyme responsible for Filamin B mRNA editing and shows that Flnb editing is tissue regulated. It gives a target-specific ADARB1-to-Flnb bridge, but the paper addresses editing more than total Flnb abundance.

citation: Stulic M, Jantsch MF. Spatio-temporal profiling of Filamin A RNA-editing reveals ADAR preferences and high editing levels outside neuronal tissues. RNA Biology. 2013;10(10):1611-1617. doi:10.4161/rna.26216.
description: This paper shows that ADARB1/ADAR2 supplies most Filamin A editing in mice and notes related substrate-specific regulation of filamin editing. It supports the filamin-family connection in Adarb1 pairs where Flnb dominates and Flna is also significant in one cell type.

citation: Hopfler M, Absmeier E, Peak-Chew SY, Vartholomaiou E, Passmore LA, Gasic I, Hegde RS. Mechanism of ribosome-associated mRNA degradation during tubulin autoregulation. Molecular Cell. 2023;83(12):2290-2302.e10. doi:10.1016/j.molcel.2023.05.020.
description: This study defines the ribosome-associated degradation mechanism that couples free tubulin sensing to tubulin mRNA decay. It is a biologically specific family-level bridge for compensatory tubulin-isotype mRNA increases after Tuba1a perturbation, although it does not directly test Tuba1a knockdown.

citation: Zhao B, Sun L, Haas M, Denenberg AG, Wong HR, Shanley TP. PP2A regulates upstream members of the c-jun N-terminal kinase mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling pathway. Shock. 2008;29(2):181-188. doi:10.1097/SHK.0b013e318070c840.
description: This paper shows that PP2A inhibition increases JNK activity and that the PP2A-A alpha structural subunit physically associates with JNK-pathway kinases. It provides a target-specific PP2A-to-JNK/AP-1 bridge for Ppp2r1a responses that include Jun induction.

citation: Perera BP, Teruyama R, Kim J. Yy1 gene dosage effect and bi-allelic expression of Peg3. PLOS ONE. 2015;10(3):e0119493. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0119493.
description: This in vivo mouse study found that half dosage of Yy1 coincided with up-regulation of Peg3 and Zim1 in the Peg3 imprinted domain, consistent with a Yy1 repressor role in mouse brain regions. It directly supports Yy1 perturbation pairs where Peg3 mRNA increased.

citation: Kim JD, Hinz AK, Choo JH, Stubbs L, Kim J. YY1 as a controlling factor for the Peg3 and Gnas imprinted domains. Genomics. 2006;89(2):262-269. doi:10.1016/j.ygeno.2006.09.009.
description: This study used Yy1 knockdown in Neuro2A cells and observed coordinated up-regulation of genes in the Peg3 imprinted domain. It supports the direction that Yy1 loss can derepress Peg3-domain transcripts.

citation: Motley A, Bright NA, Seaman MN, Robinson MS. Clathrin-mediated endocytosis in AP-2-depleted cells. Journal of Cell Biology. 2003;162(5):909-918. doi:10.1083/jcb.200305145.
description: This RNAi study shows that AP-2 depletion severely inhibits transferrin internalization, establishing AP-2 as a cargo-selective endocytic adaptor for the transferrin receptor. It supports an indirect AP2S1-to-Tfrc/endocytosis bridge without specifying Tfrc mRNA induction.

citation: Hirst J, Robinson MS. Clathrin and adaptors. Biochimica et Biophysica Acta. 1998;1404(1-2):173-193. doi:10.1016/s0167-4889(98)00056-1.
description: This review summarizes the role of the AP-2 adaptor complex in clathrin-coated vesicles budding from the plasma membrane and receptor-mediated transferrin uptake. It provides complex-level context for AP2S1, the sigma subunit of AP-2.

citation: Lee ES, Wolf EJ, Ihn SSJ, Smith HW, Emili A, Palazzo AF. TPR is required for the efficient nuclear export of mRNAs and lncRNAs from short and intron-poor genes. Nucleic Acids Research. 2020;48(20):11645-11663. doi:10.1093/nar/gkaa919.
description: This paper demonstrates that TPR depletion impairs nuclear export of a subset of mRNAs and lncRNAs downstream of NXF1 recruitment. It gives a specific TPR-to-RNA-export bridge for Tpr pairs whose central response includes RNA-processing and transport genes.

citation: Becker D, Hirsch AG, Bender L, Lingner T, Salinas G, Krebber H. Nuclear Pre-snRNA Export Is an Essential Quality Assurance Mechanism for Functional Spliceosomes. Cell Reports. 2019;27(11):3199-3214.e3. doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2019.05.031.
description: This study shows that Xpo1-dependent nuclear export of pre-snRNAs is required for proper snRNP maturation and functional spliceosome assembly in yeast. It supports an indirect XPO1-to-spliceosome bridge for Xpo1 perturbation responses containing snRNP and mRNA-export genes.

citation: Wilkinson ME, Charenton C, Nagai K. RNA Splicing by the Spliceosome. Annual Review of Biochemistry. 2020;89:359-388. doi:10.1146/annurev-biochem-091719-064225.
description: This review describes how U1, U2, and the U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP assemble and remodel the spliceosome. It supplies complex-level support for treating PRPF6, SNRNP70, and DDX23 perturbations as spliceosome insults when they elicit RNA-processing gene modules.

citation: Zhang F, Yu X. WAC, a functional partner of RNF20/40, regulates histone H2B ubiquitination and gene transcription. Molecular Cell. 2011;41(4):384-397. doi:10.1016/j.molcel.2011.01.024.
description: This paper identifies WAC as an RNF20/RNF40 partner that couples RNA polymerase II to H2B ubiquitination at active transcription sites. It supports the interpretation of Wac perturbation as a transcription-coupled chromatin insult, while leaving the direction of the neuronal-state genes indirect.

citation: Tackenberg MC, Heliodoro KM, Melink LC, Liu Y, Zhu K, Lazar MA. Normal circadian period length requires repression of Npas2 by REV-ERB nuclear receptors. Cell Reports. 2025;44(10):116437. doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2025.116437.
description: This study shows that REV-ERB nuclear receptors repress NPAS2 and CLOCK and that loss of REV-ERBs derepresses those clock transcription factors in brain and liver contexts. It directly supports Npas2 up-regulation after Nr1d1/REV-ERB alpha perturbation.

citation: Cheng LE, Zhang J, Reed RR. The transcription factor Zfp423/OAZ is required for cerebellar development and CNS midline patterning. Developmental Biology. 2007;307(1):43-52. doi:10.1016/j.ydbio.2007.04.005.
description: This mouse knockout study shows that Zfp423/OAZ is required for CNS midline patterning, cerebellar vermis development, Purkinje cell differentiation, and granule cell proliferation. It gives a cell-type and developmental bridge for Zfp423 perturbation in thalamic and cerebellar neurons but does not predict the adult transcriptional module gene by gene.

citation: Alcaraz WA, Gold DA, Raponi E, Gent PM, Concepcion D, Hamilton BA. Zfp423 controls proliferation and differentiation of neural precursors in cerebellar vermis formation. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America. 2006;103(51):19424-19429. doi:10.1073/pnas.0609184103.
description: This positional-cloning study demonstrates that Zfp423 is required for precursor proliferation, differentiation, and migration during cerebellar vermis formation. It is specific to neural development but leaves open whether acute adult Zfp423 loss should move Grid2ip, Cd47, Ntsr1, or Rab37 in the observed directions.

citation: Konig HG, Schwamborn R, Andresen S, Kinsella S, Watters O, Fenner B, Prehn JHM. NF-kappaB regulates neuronal ankyrin-G via a negative feedback loop. Scientific Reports. 2017;7:42006. doi:10.1038/srep42006.
description: This primary-neuron study connects ankyrin-G to NF-kappaB signaling at the axon initial segment and shows that Ank3 silencing increases NF-kappaB activity. It provides an indirect neuronal signaling bridge for the large Ank3 thalamic response but does not specify the Vgf, Ache, or calcium-pump transcriptional changes.
